newsitem.title: UK: HGCA head says EU feed wheat intervention possible. [CORRECTED 20:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: HGCA head says EU feed wheat intervention possible. [CORRECTED 20:50 GMT]

text.p: A senior UK grain official said on Tuesday sliding grain prices could trigger a European Union (EU) support mechanism on feed wheat that has so far been unused.
Asked whether the EU was likely to provide some kind of relief to feed wheat farmers, Tony Williams, chief executive of the Home-Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA) said: "It is possible this year."
"(But) it is very hard to read what they will do," Williams told Reuters on the sidelines of a news conference to launch HGCA's new logo.
Wheat prices have fallen some 23 percent since April on ample supplies and sagging world demand. Local losses were also due to sterling's gains in currency markets.

Feed wheat, which constitutes the majority of the British wheat harvest, does not qualify for EU intervention. But a dormant clause in EU invervention rules states that some support can be arranged if the feed wheat price declines by more than five percent to that of barley while barley is offered into intervention.
Williams said he expected "significant" offers of UK barley into intervention this year.
Feed wheat is now trading slightly above 92.50 stg a tonne, which is the level that can activate the EU support mechanism.
Williams said wheat markets were facing increased volatility. (Corrects to delete erroneous reference to size of harvests.)
"The big question is going to be, does China would come in as a major buyer or not," he said.
